pairs.difference: A Saree is one long drape with a blouse; a Lehenga is a flared skirt with a choli and dupatta.
A Kurta is an everyday long shirt; a Sherwani is the groom's long, heavy coat.
A Shawl is warm wool for winter; a Dupatta is a light scarf worn with a salwar suit.
A Salwar is gathered tight at the ankle; a Palazzo is wide, flowy and straight all the way down.
A Dhoti is tied between the legs; a Lungi is wrapped like a tube and folded up at the knee.
Dungarees have a bib and shoulder straps worn over a top; a Jumpsuit is one full piece with its own sleeves or top.
A Cap is soft cloth with a peak against the sun; a Helmet is hard, protects your head and is the law on a bike.
Sunglasses have tinted lenses for the sun; Spectacles correct your eyesight.
A Blazer has sleeves; a Waistcoat is sleeveless and worn under or instead of a jacket.
A Hairband goes over the head or around a ponytail; a Hair Clip snaps onto the hair.
A Kolhapuri is a flat leather sandal with a toe ring; a Jutti is a closed, embroidered Punjabi shoe.
Sneakers are laced and sporty; Loafers are smart slip-ons.
Jeans are blue denim; Cargo Pants are cotton with big side pockets.
A T-Shirt is short-sleeved and light; a Hoodie is warm, with a hood and a front pocket.
Boots cover the ankle and are sturdy; Heels raise the heel for parties.
A Wallet folds into a pocket for cards and cash; a Clutch is a small evening bag carried in the hand.
Both are for the monsoon. You hold an Umbrella; you wear a Raincoat.
A Sweater is knitted wool you pull over; a Jacket is outerwear with a zip or buttons.
A Gown is a long formal dress for women; a Tuxedo is a formal black suit with a bow tie for men.
A Skirt has no legs; Shorts have two.
A Belt goes round the waist; a Tie goes round the neck.
Socks are for the feet; Gloves are for the hands.
A Necklace is worn round the neck; an Anklet (payal) goes round the ankle and jingles.
Both are worn at home. A Pyjama is for sleeping; a Bathrobe is for after a bath.
A Ring goes on a finger; a Bangle goes on the wrist, often several at once.
Both go on the wrist. A Watch tells the time; a Bracelet is just jewellery.
Earrings are for the ears; a Nose Pin is for the nose.
A Handbag goes over the shoulder or arm; a Backpack goes on your back, for college or travel.
A Swimsuit is for the pool; a Tracksuit is for the gym or a morning jog.
